title: Boil-water notice: Main Street, 400–700 blocks
summary: Boil drinking water for one minute after a main repair dropped pressure below the story threshold on two blocks of Main Street.
body:
Crews repaired a cracked 8-inch main near Main and 5th (story). Pressure fell below the level where the district can guarantee no backflow, so this notice is precautionary — no contamination has been confirmed in the story.

Samples were collected this morning; the notice lifts only after two consecutive clear sample sets, which in the story takes at least 24 hours.
what_to_do: Boil for 1 minute, cool, and use for drinking, ice, brushing teeth and pet water. Showering is fine. Restaurants on the blocks should follow the health-department sheet linked at the office (story).

title: Planned outage: Elm Ridge tank cleaning
summary: Water will be off while the Elm Ridge tank is drained, inspected and cleaned. Fill a jug Monday night; pressure may be low that evening.
body:
The Elm Ridge elevated tank gets an interior inspection every five years (story). Divers found coating wear at the last check, so this outage includes a coating repair estimate.

Streets above the tank may see air in lines Tuesday evening — run a cold tap for two minutes until it clears.
what_to_do: Store a gallon per person, delay laundry, and plan on low pressure after 2pm while the tank refills.

title: Hydrant flushing: north side, week of Oct 19
summary: Overnight flushing may briefly discolor water north of Mill Creek. It is sediment, not a safety notice — run a cold tap until clear.
body:
Flushing scours mineral sediment from mains at high flow (story program). Crews work overnight street by street, north to south.

If water is discolored at breakfast, run the cold kitchen tap for two minutes. If it stays discolored past 9am, report it.
what_to_do: Avoid laundry during overnight flushing on your street if you can; check before washing whites.

title: Resolved: Low pressure near the high school
summary: A stuck pressure-reducing valve cut pressure for three hours. Replaced same day; no boil notice was needed.
body:
Operators traced low pressure to a PRV that failed closed (story). A bypass held minimum pressure while the valve was swapped.

Because pressure never fell below the boil-notice threshold, no notice was issued — this entry stays so residents who noticed it can see why.
what_to_do: Nothing now. If pressure is still low at your house, check your own pressure regulator or call for a re-read.

title: Resolved: River intake turbidity after storm
summary: Storm turbidity in the Ossel River slowed treatment for a day. Finished water met every story standard throughout; wells carried peak demand.
body:
Heavy rain muddied the river (story). The plant cut intake, leaned on wells, and increased settling time rather than pushing cloudy water through filters.

Turbidity at the tap never rose; this is published because residents asked why the river looked brown while tap water stayed clear.
what_to_do: No action. See the Q3 quality report for the turbidity numbers from that week.
